content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working on a project to measure temperature (range 20-100 Celsius) using a PT100 sensor connected to an [product_name] RTD expansion module. Additionally, an [product_name] AQ expansion module is installed, which provides the 1-10V control output based on the analog temperature input. The main goal is to send a 1-10V control signal to the analog control input AI1 of an inverter, allowing its built-in PID control to regulate cooling fans. The inverter's pinout for the 0-10V control input is shown in the attached image. I've made some connections but am unsure about their correctness. Any assistance or step-by-step guidelines would be appreciated to successfully complete this setup. Thanks.
Connect the M1 terminal of the [product_name] AQ module to the COM terminal of the inverter. Then connect the V1 terminal of the [product_name] AQ module to the AI1 terminal of the inverter.

You may also use AI2 or AI3 on the inverter's analog inputs similarly to AI1, as described by [user_name], since AI1 is often dedicated for potentiometer-based speed control. Remember, the +10V signal is meant solely for powering potentiometers. Never use it to link analog inputs and outputs between controllers. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking help to connect an [product_name] analog output module with an inverter’s analog input for temperature-based fan control. Replies outlined the correct wiring of terminals and warned against misusing the inverter’s +10V supply, but there is no confirmation that the connections work as expected. The user’s concern is avoiding miswiring and damage, and a need for clear wiring documentation or examples is evident.
analysis.user_expectations: The user looks for detailed, easy-to-follow instructions to safely connect the [product_name] AQ module to the inverter’s analog input. They want assurance that the control loop will operate correctly and safely, without placing any equipment at risk.
